gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the APsystems EZ1 is back in stock on APsystems' own US store at $325 for 900 VA (about $0.36 per VA). Two Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV 391 units, ChatGPT's 'budget' option, cost $338 at Self2Solar and give only 782 VA (about $0.43 per VA).
standout_why: I compared against solarwaypoint.com (cited, dated 2026-11-04), balconysolarkits.us/kits (cited) and pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited, dated 2026-10-18). All three list the EZ1 at $325 but call it 'sold out' on the official store, and Solar Waypoint points shoppers to a $275 reseller with limited stock. All three give the HiFlow Pro LV as a $149–$169 per-unit figure or no price at all. None works out cost per VA, and none notes that matching one EZ1's 900 VA takes two or three HiFlow units costing more. They do already cover certification scope: the CSA certificate covers the EZ1 inverter only, Hoymiles' UL 3700 status is the maker's own claim, and the EcoFlow STREAM has no UL 3700 claim. That part is not new.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pick of the APsystems EZ1-LV and removes the 'sold out' objection the rival pages raise. It also undercuts the 'budget' label ChatGPT gave the Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV. A HiFlow is only cheaper if the shopper wants a single panel and about 360–391 VA. For two panels, one EZ1 ($325, 900 VA) costs less and puts out more than two HiFlow 391s ($338, 782 VA). Enphase IQ8M is out for this question because ChatGPT's own answer says it is not meant for wall-outlet use. EcoFlow STREAM is out because no rival found a UL 3700 claim, it is on pre-order, and EcoFlow restricts plug-in use to a few states. Northern Electric Power's LIBERTY is out because its maker page shows no price and no UL 3700. Nothing Dealectric lists is a plug-in microinverter; the Sun Gold Power inverters are 48 V split-phase units, a different category.
